speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: However, we will continue to review how we can celebrate and support families.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: We have enhanced and introduced new measures in the Marriage and Parenthood package over the years to provide greater financial support for parents.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: The Government remains committed to promoting marriage and parenthood, and we will continue to review our policies to ensure they remain relevant in supporting parents.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: I had a SG58 baby, so I did not have the privilege of getting a SG50 or SG60 gift pack.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: But I know of many mothers and parents were delighted to have them.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: Would the Ministry or Government be open to exploring a pilot programme in specific regions or demographics, to assess the feasibility and impact of the Baby Gift on a smaller scale?

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: My second supplementary question will be was there any formal survey or feedback done on the impact of the Baby Gift for both the SG50 and SG60 cohorts?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: On the first suggestion to have a pilot within specific regions, have a Baby Gift on a smaller scale, just two things.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Singapore is already quite small, and I am fairly sure that if we were to give a Baby Gift to, let us say the central region, and not to the others, the other regions will very quickly put up their hands.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But I think that the more important point is this: the Baby Gift is meant to be a commemoration.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The other thing also – and we went through this when we were preparing the SG60 gift – different parents want different things.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, when we were road-testing it, some came back and said, "Can I change this gift for something else, because I already have this?" So, you will run into those issues and therefore, the general policy is we give the parents cash; they can buy what they want, but for special occasions we have something to mark that special occasion.
